# `⊂` — Enclose / Partitioned enclose

Keys: `Alt-z`. Ranks: `∞` monadic, `1 ∞` dyadic

`⊂Y` is a scalar holding `Y`.

A one-item [bracket list](brackets.qmd), `[Y]`, is a vector, not a scalar. `⊂` cannot enclose a function, because `⊂` next to a function forms a train. To enclose a function, write [`ᵘ`](../scripts.ipynb#superscripts) after it. `fᵘ` is a scalar holding `f`.

```bpl
⍴⊂1 2 3            ⍝ ⍬ₓ
↑⊂1 2 3            ⍝ 1 2 3
⊂3 ≡ 3             ⍝ $f
```

With [axes](axis.qmd), `⊂⍠K Y` encloses cells on axes `K`.

```bpl
⊂⍠1 (2 3⍴⍳6)       ⍝ [[0 1 2] [3 4 5]]
```

`N⊂Y` starts partitions at positive marks along the leading axis. Each partition is a block of major cells. Leading zero marks are ignored.

```bpl
1 0 1 0⊂"abcd"     ⍝ "ab" "cd"
1 0 1⊂3 2⍴⍳6       ⍝ [[0 1⋄2 3] [4 5⋄]]
```

A mark greater than 1 starts extra empty partitions. Unit marks extend. `N⊂⍠K Y` partitions along axis `K` instead. `N⊂⍤1 Y` partitions each row.

```bpl
1 0 1⊂⍠1 (2 3⍴⍳6)  ⍝ [[0 1⋄3 4] [[2]⋄[5]]]
1 0 1⊂⍤1 (2 3⍴⍳6)  ⍝ [[0 1] [2]⋄[3 4] [5]]
```

See also [`⊆`](nest.qmd).

## Inverse

`⊂⁻¹Y` is `↑Y`. `X⊂⁻¹Y` joins the parts `Y`. Partitioning the result by `X` must give `Y` again, so `X` can't drop leading items.

```bpl
⊂⁻¹⊂1 2             ⍝ 1 2
1 0 1⊂⁻¹(1 2⋄3)   ⍝ 1 2 3
```
